t: Delhi was built, destroyed and rebuilt several times, and tradition counts seven cities on its site, from the Tomara fort of 1052 to Shah Jahan’s Shahjahanabad.
It was the capital of the Delhi Sultanate from 1206 and of the Mughal Empire from 1638, and it was sacked by Timur in 1398 and by Nader Shah in 1739.
Britain moved its Indian capital to Delhi in 1911, and after Partition in 1947 the city changed from a Mughal city to a Punjabi one.
dyk: Excavations at Purana Qila, which tradition identifies with the Indraprastha of the Mahabharata, have found painted grey pottery of the 11th century BCE but no sign of a built environment or fortifications.
ev: Anang Pal of the Tomara dynasty builds Lal Kot
Qutb-ud-din Aibak founds the Delhi Sultanate with Delhi as its capital
Shah Jahan makes Shahjahanabad the Mughal capital
Nader Shah sacks and loots the city
Rebels hold Delhi until British troops retake it in September
The capital of British India is announced to be moving to Delhi
New Delhi becomes the capital of independent India

f.founded: Anang Pal of the Tomara dynasty built Lal Kot in 1052 CE; the Tomaras are placed earlier too, and tradition links the site with Indraprastha, the city of the Mahabharata.
f.where: On the Yamuna river, chiefly on its right bank, between the Yamuna floodplains and the Delhi Ridge, in northern India.
f.known: Capital of the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughal Empire; the Qutub Minar, the Red Fort and Humayun’s Tomb; Sufism and qawwali; Urdu poetry; the sacks of 1398 and 1739; the rebellion of 1857; New Delhi, the capital of India
f.today: Delhi is the National Capital Territory of India and contains New Delhi, the capital of the country.
